## Osteosarcoma Clinical Trial in Dogs

Current Status: Open and enrolling
Principal Investigators: 【73†Dara L. Kraitchman, V.M.D., Ph.D., F.A.C.C.†profiles.hopkinsmedicine.org】, 【74†[email protected]】

To find out more about this clinical trial, send an email to 【75†[email protected]】 or call 410-502-7325.

  * ### [Button: Summary]
To assess the effectiveness of cryoablation or an investigational immunotherapy to treat osteosarcoma of the appendicular skeleton. Cryoablation is a technique to freeze tumors that may kill the tumor, alleviate pain, and assist the body in rejecting cancer that has spread. Immunotherapy is used as a means to create an in-situ cancer vaccine towards the tumor. Either treatment is performed prior to amputation.

  * ### [Button: Funding and Support]
The cryotherapy or immunotherapy and imaging to look for cancer spread or metastasis is fully funded. Any medications our veterinarians prescribe to alleviate the side effects of the procedure, as well as follow-up imaging and blood tests will also be covered by the study. Amputation and chemotherapy are required and are not covered by the study.

  * ### [Button: Trial Eligibility]

Dogs of any breed, sex, and age are eligible for the study.

  * ### [Button: Inclusion Criteria]
    * The dog’s owner has the ability to understand and sign a written informed consent and is willing to comply with study protocol.
    * Histopathological confirmation of osteosarcoma.
    * Systemically healthy other than the diagnosis of osteosarcoma.
    * No prior treatment for osteosarcoma or chemotherapy for other cancers.
    * Ability to transport dog to CIGAT for treatment and follow-up visits
    * Other restrictions may apply. Please call for details.

  * ### [Button: Exclusion Criteria]
    * Dogs who have previously received chemotherapy or other investigational agents.
    * Dog who is participating in another study.
    * Life-threatening medical or immunosuppressive illness unrelated to cancer.
    * Evidence of serious systemic disorder or other condition that is clinically incompatible with the study.

  * ### [Button: Trial Timeline]
Eligible dogs will receive a PET-CT scan and will receive cryotherapy alone or two doses of tumor-injected immunotherapy.  Amputation is required at approximately 2 weeks after treatment followed by chemotherapy.  CT or PET-CT scans will be obtained at 3, 6, and 12 months after treatment Further monitoring will be performed as deemed necessary by CIGAT veterinarians.
## Canine Brain Cancer Clinical Trial

Study Title: Radiation Therapy Combined with Chemotherapy In Dogs with Brain Tumors
Current Status: Open and enrolling
Principal Investigators: 【73†Dara L. Kraitchman, V.M.D., Ph.D., F.A.C.C.†profiles.hopkinsmedicine.org】, 【76†[email protected]】

To find out more about this clinical trial, send an email to 【77†[email protected]】 or call 410-502-7325.

  * ### [Button: Summary]
To assess the effectiveness of standard of care radiation therapy combined with chemotherapy dogs with suspected gliomas.  In people radiation therapy (RT) is combined with a chemotherapy given by mouth called tetrazolamide (TMZ) to treat glioblastoma.

  * ### [Button: Funding and Support]
The radiation therapy and chemotherapy will be fully funded. Any medications our veterinarians prescribe to alleviate the side effects of the procedure, as well as follow-up MRI imaging and blood tests will also be covered by the study.  Treatment for progression of disease is not covered by the study.

  * ### [Button: Trial Eligibility]

Dogs of any breed and sex are eligible for the study.

  * ### [Button: Inclusion Criteria:]
    * The dog’s owner has the ability to understand and sign a written informed consent and is willing to comply with study protocol.
    * Intra-axial brain tumor (suspect glioma) >1cm in size on MRI, restricted to one side of the brain.
    * Age of at least 1 year.
    * Ability to transport dog to CIGAT for radiation therapy and follow-up visits
    * Other restrictions may apply. Please call for details.

  * ### [Button: Exclusion Criteria]
    * Anticipated life expectancy of less than 1 month.
    * Previous or current oncological treatment of the brain tumor.
    * Participation in another study.
    * Evidence of serious systemic disorder or other condition that is clinically incompatible with the study.

  * ### [Button: Trial Timeline]
Eligible dogs will receive a CT scan under general anesthesia for RT planning. RT will be performed on five consecutive workdays with concurrent administration of TMZ.  We will perform the follow-up MRI scans at various intervals up to 1 year after treatment free of charge. Further monitoring will be performed as deemed necessary by CIGAT veterinarians.
## Canine Hemangiosarcoma Clinical Trial

Study Title: The Effect of an Investigative Agent on Progression of Residual Disease in Canine Hemangiosarcoma
Current Status: Closed
Principal Investigators: 【73†Dara L. Kraitchman, V.M.D., Ph.D., F.A.C.C.†profiles.hopkinsmedicine.org】, 【78†[email protected]】

This clinical trial is currently closed to new enrollment.

To find out more about this clinical trial, send an email to 【79†[email protected]】 or call 410-502-7325.

  * ### [Button: Summary]
This is a clinical trial that will enroll a total of nine dogs in order to evaluate the effects of an FDA-approved investigative agent on dogs that have hemangiosarcoma (visceral and/or cutaneous). Safety and toxicology studies have been performed in healthy dogs. This is the first trial using the agent for treating canine hemangiosarcoma.

  * ### [Button: Selection of Participants]
Eligible dogs will have undergone histopathologic evaluation of their tumor at their local veterinary hospital. Following visceral or cutaneous diagnosis of hemangiosarcoma, the patient may be considered for enrollment. Dogs should weigh more than 10 kg (22 lbs) to be eligible for participation and be older than 1 year of age. Preoperative medical records, radiographs, ultrasounds, complete blood counts, serum chemistries and urinalyses will help us determine if dogs are eligible for this trial.
In addition, each pet owner must sign an informed consent form in order to participate in the clinical trial.
Participating dogs should meet the following criteria:

    * The owner is willing to comply with all study procedures and be available for the duration of the study
    * The patient should have no concurrent kidney, liver or heart disease, or problems with blood clotting
    * The patient should have no heart-based tumors

  * ### [Button: Procedures]
    1. Splenectomy or lobectomy or histopathologic confirmation - the surgery is not part of the study; the surgery and diagnostic fees are paid by the owner
    2. After confirmation of hemangiosarcoma, the study will provide a PET-CT scan (whole body) to determine the dog's baseline tumor burden as well as a blood test to check for a mutation in the MDR1 gene
    3. Dogs with metastatic tumors measured by PET-CT scan are eligible for enrollment
    4. Chemotherapy: the first chemotherapy will be given within one week of the initial PET-CT scan. A second chemotherapy session will be given one week later. During week three, there will be no treatment. This cycle will be repeated two more times for a total of six chemotherapy sessions. Prior to every chemotherapy session, blood tests will be performed
    5. Follow-up PET-CT scan will be performed after chemotherapy has finished
    6. Once a month physical examination will be performed (this may include blood tests, radiographs and/or ultrasound) for 2-3 more visits after chemotherapy has concluded
  * ### [Button: Cost of Studies]

Owners are responsible for their dog's initial surgery (workup). The study pays for all diagnostics and therapies that occur at the Center for Image-Guided Animal Therapy including the MDR1 genetic test, PET-CT scans, chemotherapy, lab work, and physical examinations.

家里狗狗确诊肥大细胞瘤、骨肉瘤、口腔鳞癌？

各位接诊此类病例的宠物医师请注意！

中农董军实验室抗肿瘤新药临床试验正式开启全国招募，符合条件的患病犬可免费使用抗肿瘤新药。

本次临床试验，既能大幅减轻宠物主人高额用药的经济压力，同时也会为犬类肿瘤治疗研发更安全有效的全新方案。

诚邀全国宠物医生积极推荐适配病例，也欢迎患病犬主咨询报名，推动小动物肿瘤诊疗水平持续提升。

试验组1：犬肥大细胞瘤

肿瘤状态：未截肢/肺部转移

试验组3：犬口腔鳞癌

本次试验为新药初步临床效果研究，通过规范给药、定期复查监测，客观评估抗肿瘤药物对口腔鳞癌的临床效果治疗新方案。

参与福利
1.试验周期内，抗肿瘤新药免费使用，无需承担药费；

2.全程实验室专业技术团队跟进，定期免费肿瘤相关指标复查、病灶评估；

犬只入组要求（带瘤病例）

1.确诊依据：经组织病理检测确诊为肥大细胞瘤 / 骨肉瘤 / 口腔鳞癌（需提供病理报告）；

2.年龄：1 岁以上，无严重心肝肾衰竭、重度贫血等终末期基础重病；

3.主人配合度：可按要求按时送犬复查、配合采血、病灶影像学记录，完整完成全试验周期；

试验流程

1.报名登记：医师 / 主人联系对接人，提交病理报告、犬只基础病历；

2.初筛评估：实验室审核病例，确认符合入组标准后通知；

3.基线检查：入组前完成基础血液、肿瘤病灶基线检测；

4.规范给药：按照试验方案免费提供新药， 院内给药；

5.定期随访复查：固定周期检测病灶大小、血液指标，记录药物反应与肿瘤情况；

# 犬肿瘤mRNA个体化免疫疗法 — 研究详情与入组标准

谁能入组、流程怎么走、费用怎么算——入组前先看懂这些

犬肿瘤mRNA个体化免疫疗法IIT研究，是宝科雅（PETcura）发起并资助的研究者发起多中心临床转化研究（IIT），联合创模生物与前沿mRNA技术研发机构，探索为犬类恶性肿瘤患犬定制个体化mRNA免疫制剂的安全性、可行性与初步疗效。本项目为探索性研究，不是已获批上市的商业化兽药产品。

研究状态：限额招募中——目前在北京、上海、广州、杭州、南京、深圳、沈阳、成都、重庆9个城市、12家合作医院开展入组评估。
## 研究目的

  1. 通过超高深度RNA测序（≥50G）精准鉴定犬肿瘤特异性新生抗原（含基因突变、基因融合、可变剪接）
  2. 为每只患犬定制个体化mRNA-LNP免疫制剂
  3. 激发新生抗原特异性CD8⁺ T细胞免疫应答
  4. 验证"5针密集初免+淋巴结休整+3针强化"共8针给药方案的安全性
  5. 建立系统化给药前基线、全程采血监测及末次给药后综合评估的标准化检测体系
## 入组标准（须全部满足）

  * 病理确诊：组织学或细胞学确诊的犬类恶性肿瘤（实体瘤及淋巴瘤等；排除T细胞淋巴瘤、脑瘤）
  * 年龄体重：年龄≥2岁；体重≥5kg（小型犬可个案评估，如泰妮）
  * 样本可获取：可获取新鲜肿瘤组织及配对癌旁正常组织（手术当天留取）
  * 体况达标：由主治医生评估体况（改良ECOG≤2）与肝肾血液指标（ALT/AST < 3×ULN，肌酐 < 2×ULN，Hb > 80 g/L）
  * LNP肌注耐受度评估通过：注射与制剂相同LNP体系的测试制剂，院内留观1小时无全身性过敏反应（入组必要条件）
  * 知情同意：主人充分知情并签署知情同意书，能配合完成全程观察与采血

> 排除：T细胞淋巴瘤、脑瘤；近2周内接受化疗/放疗/大剂量皮质激素；合并严重感染、自身免疫病或免疫缺陷；妊娠哺乳期；预期生存期<6个月。
## 治疗与随访时间线

阶段  | 内容  | 时间
--- | --- | ---
入组评估  | 病理确诊 + 肌注耐受评估 + 体况血检 + 知情同意  | 术前或术后完成
T0 采样  | 手术当天留取肿瘤组织+癌旁组织，冷链送检  | 手术当天
T1–T6 制备  | 病理确认 → RNA测序（约2周）→ 新抗原分析与序列设计 → 制剂合成与LNP包裹、质检放行  | 取样后约7–9周
D0–D28  | 密集初免：5针，每周1次（大腿外侧肌注，固定20 µg/0.5 mL）  | 5周
D29–D41  | 淋巴结休整期  | 14天
D42–D84  | 强化免疫：3针，每3周1次  | 6周
D85–D99  | 末次全面评估（安全性+影像/体表测量）  | —
长期  | 定期随访（治疗后1–2个月首次影像评估，后续定期）  | 长期
## 安全性设计

  * 耐受评估：入组前LNP肌注耐受度评估，院内留观1小时，阳性（全身性过敏反应）一次排除
  * 全程监测：每次注射前血常规+肝肾功能，记录体温、精神、食欲
  * 急救预案：注射医院须备妥抢救车（肾上腺素、抗组胺药、地塞米松等），每次注射后留观≥1小时
  * AE分级处理：轻度记录观察、中度暂缓下一针、重度/SAE立即停止并上报，全程由医生主导处置
  * 禁忌提醒：D0–D84期间禁止使用大剂量糖皮质激素（会破坏免疫激活），急救情况例外

## 兜底交付

所有完成RNA测序的病例，无论是否找到新抗原，均可获得一份靶向药用药指南报告——基于肿瘤分子特征提供潜在药物方向参考（不构成处方，供主治兽医结合临床判断）。

## 费用分担

主人承担取样冻存、测序相关的部分服务费用；mRNA定制制剂的设计与制备由宝科雅作为项目发起方全额资助。具体费用构成在入组评估时由项目组与医生详细说明。本研究为探索性研究：付费不等于自动入组，入组批准权保留在项目方。
## 数据与隐私

病例数据仅用于项目内部分析与阶段性复盘；经主人授权后，脱敏数据可用于学术论文、会议报告与宣传材料。项目未来发表的学术成果，参与医生作为联合发起人共同署名。

重要说明：本项目不替代标准治疗，是建立在主治兽医治疗方案之上的附加探索。入组批准权保留在项目方，付费不等于自动入组。退出规则以知情同意书约定为准（疾病自然进展导致的退出有相应豁免条款）。

# ReachGlio: nuevo ensayo clínico para perros con glioma de alto grado

17 septiembre, 2026 【12†Hospital Veterinario Puchol】 【13†Neurologia】

【14†Image: resonancia magnetica neurologia-glioma】

El Hospital Veterinario Puchol ha iniciado el reclutamiento de pacientes para ReachGlio, un Ensayo Clínico Veterinario dirigido a perros con diagnóstico presuntivo de glioma de alto grado, uno de los tumores cerebrales más complejos en neurología y oncología veterinaria.
El estudio ha sido autorizado por laAgencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios (AEMPS)y está financiado en el marco de la convocatoria europea TRANSCAN-3, orientada a impulsar la investigación traslacional en cáncer.

El Ensayo Clínico Veterinario se desarrollará en elHospital Veterinario Puchol, en el marco de un proyecto de investigación promovido por la Unidad de Neurooncología del Instituto de Salud Carlos III, y coordinado por la Universidad Camilo José Cela.
Más allá de evaluar una nueva estrategia terapéutica en el contexto de un ensayo clínico, ReachGlio busca responder a una pregunta especialmente relevante en neurooncología:

¿Podemos conseguir que los tratamientos antitumorales lleguen de forma más eficaz a las células tumoradas en el cerebro?

【15†Image】Isidro Mateo y Rafaela Draque en intervención quirúrgica (Servicio de Neurología HV Puchol)
## Glioma en perros: uno de los grandes retos de la neurología veterinaria

Los gliomas son tumores primarios del sistema nervioso central que se originan a partir de células de estirpe glial. Dentro de este grupo se incluyen fundamentalmente a los oligodendrogliomas y los astrocitomas.

Aparecen principalmente en perros adultos o geriátricos y se ha descrito una mayor predisposición en determinadas razas, especialmente entre las braquicéfalas.
Si nos preguntamos cuales son los síntomas de un tumor cerebral en un perro, estos dependen de la localización y extensión del tumor. Entre las manifestaciones que pueden aparecer se encuentran:

  * crisis epilépticas de nueva aparición;
  * cambios de comportamiento;
  * alteraciones del nivel de consciencia;
  * desorientación;
  * alteraciones de la marcha;
  * déficits neurológicos focales.
【16†Image】Glioma presente en perros y humanos
En un perro adulto, la aparición de una primera crisis epiléptica o de otros signos neurológicos progresivos puede justificar una valoración neurológica especializada y la realización de pruebas de diagnóstico por imagen, entre ellas la resonancia magnética cerebral.
## El papel de la resonancia magnética

La resonancia magnética cerebral en perros es una herramienta fundamental para identificar y caracterizar una masa intracraneal y, en combinación con la evaluación clínica, permite establecer un diagnóstico diferencial muy específico de glioma de alto grado.

Sin embargo, la clasificación definitiva del tumor requiere su estudio histopatológico.

【14†Image】Resonancia magnética cerebral compatible con glioma
La barrera hematoencefálica: cuando el propio cerebro dificulta el tratamiento

Uno de los principales desafíos del tratamiento farmacológico del tumor cerebral en perros es labarrera hematoencefálica.

Se trata de un sistema de protección esencial que regula de manera muy estricta el paso de determinadas sustancias desde la sangre hacia el tejido nervioso.
Esa protección, imprescindible para el funcionamiento normal del cerebro, supone también un desafío terapéutico: algunos medicamentos pueden tener dificultades para alcanzar concentraciones terapéuticas en los tumores cerebrales o gliomas caninos.

Además, ésta barrera hematoencefálica no es uniforme en todo el tumor, algunas zonas pueden ser más permeables, mientras que otras continúan limitando significativamente la entrada de determinados tratamientos.
Por tanto, conseguir que un fármaco llegue al cerebro no significa necesariamente que alcance de manera suficiente todas las áreas relevantes del tumor.

Este es precisamente uno de los retos que investiga ReachGlio.
## ¿Qué estudia exactamente ReachGlio?

El Ensayo Clínico Veterinario evaluará una estrategia basada en la administración deSNGR-TNF en combinación con temozolomida.

Según el protocolo del estudio, SNGR-TNF es un agente dirigido a la vasculatura tumoral cuya finalidad es inducir una modificación transitoria y controlada de la barrera hematoencefálica.
El objetivo es estudiar si esta modificación puede favorecer una mayor penetración de la temozolomida, el principal quimioterápico utilizado para el tratamiento de glioma canino y humano de alto grado.

Por tanto, ReachGlio no evalúa únicamente un nuevo esquema de tratamiento. Su planteamiento científico consiste en estudiar si es posiblemodificar temporalmente las condiciones de acceso al tumor para favorecer la exposición al fármaco.
Se trata de un ensayo piloto de naturaleza exploratoria, por lo que uno de sus principales objetivos será obtener información sobre farmacodinamia, tolerabilidad y seguridad que permita orientar futuras fases de investigación.
## Un diseño con ajuste dinámico de dosis

Otro de los aspectos relevantes del estudio es su diseño.

ReachGlio utilizará un modelo secuencial con ajuste dinámico de dosis, en el que las decisiones se tomarán teniendo en cuenta parámetros de seguridad y biomarcadores farmacodinámicos.

Este planteamiento permite incorporar la información obtenida progresivamente durante el ensayo y ajustar la dosis de acuerdo con los criterios de seguridad y los datos farmacodinámicos establecidos en el protocolo.
La autorización de la AEMPS implica además que el estudio debe desarrollarse bajo un protocolo previamente definido, con requisitos específicos de seguridad, seguimiento, documentación y bienestar animal.
## ¿Qué perros pueden ser candidatos?

ReachGlio está dirigido aperros con diagnóstico presuntivo de glioma de alto grado y un peso corporal igual o superior a 7 kg, que además cumplan los criterios establecidos en el protocolo del estudio.

La identificación de un posible candidato comienza mucho antes de la inclusión en el estudio.
El papel del veterinario generalista y del veterinario remitente resulta especialmente importante ante pacientes que presentan signos compatibles con enfermedad prosencefálica, especialmente:

  * crisis epilépticas de nueva aparición en un perro adulto
  * cambios conductuales
  * alteración del estado mental
  * déficits neurológicos focales
Tras la evaluación neurológica y las pruebas de diagnóstico por imagen correspondientes, los pacientes que presenten hallazgos compatibles con los criterios iniciales podrán ser valorados individualmente para estudiar su posible inclusión en el estudio.

【17†Image】Imagen histológica de tejido tumoral compatible con glioma.
## ¿Qué implica participar en ReachGlio?

Los perros incluidos recibirán seis ciclos de tratamiento, con un intervalo de 21 días entre cada ciclo.

El protocolo contempla visitas al Hospital Veterinario Puchol para la administración intravenosa del tratamiento y su monitorización, junto con medicación oral en domicilio.

El seguimiento incluirá:
  * evaluaciones neurológicas periódicas;
  * controles analíticos;
  * resonancias magnéticas con contraste para valoración de los cambios en el tumor;
  * monitorización de posibles efectos adversos;
  * y valoración de la evolución de la lesión.

El protocolo contempla también la confirmación histopatológica post mortem del tumor, realizada por laboratorios especializados.

【18†Image】Glioma cerebral observado en necropsia.
Aunque este aspecto requiere una comunicación especialmente sensible con las familias, permite obtener información muy valiosa para la investigación, ya que hace posible relacionar los hallazgos de la resonancia magnética y la evolución clínica con las características histológicas del tumor. Esta información es imprescindible para comprender mejor la enfermedad y, particularmente, para interpretar los resultados obtenidos durante el ensayo.
## El Hospital Veterinario Puchol desarrollará la fase clínica veterinaria

La incorporación del Hospital Veterinario Puchol al proyecto permitirá trasladar esta investigación al contexto clínico, trabajando con pacientes caninos con tumores que aparecen de forma espontánea, dentro de un entorno clínico especializado y bajo un protocolo específicamente autorizado.
El hospital será el centro encargado de desarrollar el ensayo clínico, con participación de su Servicio de Neurología y de los recursos necesarios para la evaluación clínica, el diagnóstico por imagen, la administración del tratamiento y el seguimiento de los pacientes.
Los procedimientos específicamente contemplados dentro del protocolo de investigación, incluyendo el tratamiento, las resonancias de seguimiento y las analíticas vinculadas al estudio, están financiados en el marco de TRANSCAN-3 y no supondrán un coste adicional para los propietarios.

Sin embargo, el principal valor de este proyecto no es económico.
ReachGlio representa la posibilidad de que determinados pacientes con una enfermedad neurológica grave accedan a una estrategia terapéutica experimental única dentro de un Ensayo Clínico regulado, protocolizado y estrechamente monitorizado, pudiéndose beneficiar de las nuevas oportunidades terapéuticas que ofrecen moléculas actualmente en desarrollo

Y representa también algo esencial para el futuro de la medicina veterinaria: seguir generando evidencia allí donde todavía existen preguntas sin respuesta.
### Información para veterinarios

El reclutamiento de pacientes comenzó el 1 de septiembre de 2026.

Los veterinarios que atiendan a un perro con una lesión intracraneal compatible con un glioma de alto grado pueden contactar con el Hospital Veterinario Puchol para valorar conjuntamente si el paciente cumple inicialmente los criterios necesarios para ser considerado candidato al ensayo.
La puesta en marcha de ReachGlio supone un nuevo paso en el compromiso del Hospital Veterinario Puchol con una medicina basada en la especialización, el rigor científico, la innovación y la investigación clínica, especialmente en enfermedades complejas en las que todavía es necesario seguir avanzando.

### 治験・臨床試験情報案内

#### 犬のリンパ系腫瘍に対する抗CD20抗体による臨床試験

  * 犬のリンパ系腫瘍（リンパ腫、白血病など）に対する新規治療法として、抗CD20抗体による臨床試験を行っております。
  * この治療法は、通常の抗がん剤治療とは異なり、分子標的療法に分類されます。
抗CD20抗体は、医療ではリツキサン®という名前の薬剤が1998年よりすでに使用されており、リンパ腫などの患者さんに対して多大な貢献をしている薬ですが、これを【30†我々の研究室において†www.mizutakuvet.com】犬用に独自に開発した同様の薬剤です。
  * 対象となる腫瘍、試験内容などについての条件がございますので、ご興味ある方は水野（mizutaku@yamaguchi-u.ac.jp）までご一報いただきますよう宜しくお願い致します。
#### 犬の免疫介在性疾患に対する他家脂肪由来幹細胞による臨床試験

  * 犬のさまざまな難治性免疫介在性疾患に対する新規治療法として、他家脂肪由来幹細胞を用いた臨床試験を行っております。
  * この治療法は、再生医療に分類される新しい治療法で、脂肪由来幹細胞によって免疫調節することを目的としております。アニコム先進医療研究所株式会社（【31†https://www.anicom.co.jp†www.anicom.co.jp】）との共同で行っております。
  * 対象となる疾患、試験内容などについての条件がございますので、ご興味ある方は水野（mizutaku@yamaguchi-u.ac.jp）までご一報いただきますよう宜しくお願い致します。
#### 犬の腫瘍（がん）の早期診断に関する臨床研究

  * 犬の様々な腫瘍（がん）を早期に検出すること、また、再発を予測することを目的とした臨床研究を行っています。
  * 研究にご提供いただくものは血液のみであり、実現すれば動物へのダメージを最小限に抑えた腫瘍検査を行うことができるようになると期待されます。
  * 対象となるのは腫瘍性疾患または感染・炎症性疾患の犬です。貧血または3kgを下回る体重の犬は、採血の影響を考慮して研究対象外としています。
  * その他、本研究のより詳しい情報についてのお問い合わせは上林（s-kam@yamaguchi-u.ac.jp）までご連絡ください。
#### 犬の腫瘍（がん）に対する免疫チェックポイント分子（PD-1）阻害抗体による臨床試験

  * 犬の様々な腫瘍（がん）に対する新規治療法として、免疫チェックポイント分子（PD-1）阻害抗体による臨床試験を行っております。
  * これまでの外科治療、抗がん剤治療、放射線治療とは全く異なる新しい治療法であり、分子標的療法に分類されます。抗PD-1抗体は、医療ではオプジーボ®、キートルーダ®という名前の薬剤としてがん治療に用いられていますが、【30†我々の研究室において†www.mizutakuvet.com】犬用に独自開発した同様の薬剤を用います。
  * 対象となる腫瘍、試験内容などについての条件がございますので、ご興味ある方は水野（mizutaku@yamaguchi-u.ac.jp）までご一報いただきますよう宜しくお願い致します。

## Terapias baseadas em vírus oncolíticos para câncer em animais

.

### PESQUISADORES DO LOCT

【6†Image】

###### médica veterinária
### Amanda da Matta Santos

..

    * Médica veterinária pela UFG.

    * Mestranda pela FZEA - USP no Programa de Pós-graduação em Biociência Animal.

.

O projeto tem como foco o desenvolvimento de um vírus geneticamente modificado para o tratamento do melanoma oral em cães. Esse vírus atua destruindo diretamente as células tumorais e, por meio da expressão de quimiocinas, promove o recrutamento de células do sistema imune, potencializando a resposta contra o câncer.

.
【7†CNPQ – Currículo Lattes†lattes.cnpq.br】

【8†Image】

### Carolina Mariano Beraldo

..

    * Médica veterinária pela FZEA - USP.

    * Doutoranda pela FZEA - USP no Programa de Pós-graduação em Biociência Animal.

.

Ensaio clínico de fase I destinado a avaliar a segurança e a dose ideal do vírus oncolítico NDV em até 20 cães com câncer. O vírus tem ação seletiva, destruindo células tumorais sem afetar células saudáveis. Serão analisados parâmetros de segurança e os efeitos terapêuticos antitumorais.

.

## Ongoing Clinical Trial

## Autologous Cancer Vaccine with Checkpoint Inhibitor for Treatment of Canine Osteosarcoma
### Study Purpose

This study is evaluating the safety and effectiveness of K9-ACV, a canine cancer vaccine made from a dog’s own tumor cells, combined with a novel checkpoint inhibitor (CD200AR-L). The study will compare this new approach to standard chemotherapy in dogs diagnosed with appendicular osteosarcoma (a type of bone cancer).
### About the Study

This is a randomized clinical study. All dogs will undergo limb amputation as part of standard care. After surgery, dogs will be randomly assigned to one of two treatment groups:

K9-ACV Vaccine Group: Dogs receive an immune checkpoint inhibitor followed by three doses of the personalized vaccine, spaced three weeks apart.
Chemotherapy Group: Dogs receive standard carboplatin chemotherapy every three weeks for four total treatments. Dogs in both groups will return for follow-up visits at 4, 6, and 8 months for physical exams, lab work, and imaging.
### Who Can Participate

Dogs may be eligible if they:

  * Are at least 1 year old and weigh 20 kg or more
  * Have confirmed Stage IIB appendicular osteosarcoma
  * Are otherwise in good general health

Dogs may not be eligible if they:

  * Have received immunotherapy, chemotherapy, or immune-modulating drugs within 30 days
  * Are pregnant, lactating, or intended for breeding
  * Are currently enrolled in another clinical study
### Potential Benefits

  * A chance to receive a novel immunotherapy
  * Increased survival time
  * Improved quality of life
### Potential Risks

As with any medical treatment, side effects are possible.

Immunotherapy – local redness, swelling, or pain around the injection site; mild fever, lethargy; nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, reduced appetite; rare risk of severe allergic reaction that would require anti-inflammatory therapy.
Chemotherapy – bone marrow suppression (low white cell or platelet counts); gastrointestinal upset (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea); fever, lethargy. If untreated for bone marrow suppression, rarely dogs could become septic and require intensive antibiotic therapy.
### Study Outcomes

Primary Outcome:

  * Disease-Free Interval measured by chest x-rays at 8 months or upon disease progression

Secondary Outcomes:

  * Quality of Life assessments using validated veterinary tools
  * Monitoring of any side effects or adverse events
### Additional Information

All dogs must pass a prescreening process that includes a physical exam, lab work, x-rays, and an ultrasound. Enrollment requires a commitment to follow-up visits for at least 8 months. The study team will work closely with you to monitor your dog’s health and provide updates throughout the study.

This clinical trial is designed in accordance with USDA CVB VSM 100.121

### Essais cliniques et traitements innovants
# Essais cliniques et traitements innovants

Tout au long de l'année, des essais cliniques sont mis en œuvre afin d'améliorer la prise en charge des animaux de compagnie. L'EnvA, dans ses cliniques, propose aux propriétaires d'en bénéficier en participant à des études.
Ophtalmologie

Une étude clinique pour un nouveau traitement médical de la cataracte diabétique chez le chien menée à l'hôpital des animaux de compagnie.
L’équipe d’ophtalmologie recrute des chiens diabétiques pour une étude clinique dont l’objectif est de tester l’efficacité d’un nouveau traitement médical de la cataracte associée au diabète sucré chez le chien.
La cataracte, qui correspond à une opacification plus ou moins complète du cristallin, est la complication oculaire du diabète sucré la plus fréquente chez le chien. Lorsqu’elle évolue, le chien perd la vision. Actuellement, seul un traitement chirurgical peut permettre une récupération de la vision. Mais certains chiens ne peuvent pas bénéficier du traitement chirurgical, qui est onéreux et qui nécessite une anesthésie générale.
Pour cette raison, l’EnvA travaille en collaboration avec une équipe de chercheurs de l’université de Gand (Belgique) pour tester l’efficacité clinique d’un traitement médical, sous forme de collyre, qui a pour but de réduire l’opacification du cristallin lors de cataracte diabétique chez le chien.
Il s’agit d’un traitement administré sous forme de collyre pendant une durée de trois mois. Les chiens inclus dans l’étude bénéficieront d’un examen oculaire complet tous les mois pendant la durée de l’étude. Tous les frais des examens liés à l’étude seront pris en charge par l'hôpital des animaux de compagnie.

Endocrinologie
Le "système rénine-angiotensine-aldostérone" désigne le principal système permettant la régulation de la pression artérielle et de la concentration en potassium dans le sang chez les mammifères. Certaines maladies (hormonales, rénales ou cardiaques par exemple) peuvent conduire à une activation anormale de ce système : on parle alors d’hyperaldostéronisme. Parmi ces maladies, l’hyperaldostéronisme primaire est défini par une sécrétion dérégulée et autonome d’aldostérone par les glandes surrénales.
Malgré ses répercussions pouvant être graves (cécité, atteinte rénale, manifestations musculaires), il est probable que cette entité soit sous-diagnostiquée.
L’équipe du service de médecine interne de l【1†'hôpital des animaux de compagnie de l'EnvA】 travaille sur la caractérisation des hyperaldostéronismes primaires et secondaires, afin d’en améliorer la reconnaissance et le diagnostic chez le chat. A ce titre, l’EnvA recrute des chats présentant les affections suivantes :
- un hyperaldostéronisme primaire suspecté ou confirmé (masse surrénalienne associée à une hypertension artérielle et/ou une hypokaliémie),
- une hypertension artérielle essentielle (dite également idiopathique),
- une maladie susceptible de causer un hyperaldostéronisme secondaire (hyperthyroïdie, maladie rénale chronique).
Les animaux inclus dans l’étude bénéficieront d’un examen sanguin et urinaire exhaustif, de mesures de la pression artérielle, d’un examen du fond d’œil, d’un examen échocardiographique et d’une échographie abdominale visant à caractériser la maladie dont ils souffrent. Pour bénéficier de l'inclusion, les animaux ne doivent pas recevoir de traitement avant leur présentation.
L’inclusion dans le protocole permet aux propriétaires de bénéficier de réductions financières grâce à une bourse scientifique accordée par le TRIG (Translational RAAS Interest Group).

Gastro-entérologie


Une étude est en cours à l'école nationale vétérinaire d'Alfort afin d’optimiser la prise en charge des entéropathies exsudatives, maladie complexe dont le pronostic peut être sombre. Les spécialistes de l'hôpital des animaux de compagnie recrutent des chiens avec entéropathies exsudatives dans le cadre d'une étude afin de mieux comprendre cette affection.
La prise en charge des chiens a donc pour objectif d’améliorer le pronostic en proposant une alimentation ciblée et un suivi régulier.
L'EnvA recrute ainsi tout chien présentant une hypo-albuminémie et/ou des troubles digestifs.

L'étude n'entraine aucun risque supplémentaire pour l'animal et permet un suivi gratuit durant plusieurs semaines.
Cancérologie
Le cancer est une préoccupation majeure pour les propriétaires d’animaux de compagnie. En effet, près d’un chien sur deux de plus de 10 ans en est atteint. Les avancées permanentes dans le diagnostic et le traitement des cancers en médecine vétérinaire ont permis d’améliorer l’espérance et la qualité de vie de nos animaux.
Pourtant, malgré les progrès importants réalisés dans ce domaine, de nouveaux traitements sont nécessaires. Ainsi, afin que nos animaux bénéficient des nouveautés diagnostiques et thérapeutiques nous proposons la participation à des essais cliniques.
### Recrutements chiens avec tumeurs colorectales

A l’aide d’un prélèvement de selles et d’une biopsie par endoscopie, les vétérinaires de l'EnvA confirment le diagnostic de cancer colorectal chez le chien et souhaitent améliorer le dépistage précoce de cette maladie chez le chien mais aussi chez l’Homme. Une collaboration est en cours avec le Pr Tony Lefebvre, Université Lille 1.

## Recrutement pour un essai clinique multicentrique pour le traitement par cimentation des ostéosarcomes appendiculaires chez le chien.

Les cliniciens du Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Vétérinaire d’Oniris et la société TheraVet ® réalisent actuellement une étude clinique prospective multicentrique sur le traitement de l’ostéosarcome du chien avec un ciment osseux injectable (BIOCERA-VET®).

### Qu’est-ce que l’ostéosarcome ?
#### 【4†Descriptif de la maladie】

L’ostéosarcome est le cancer des os le plus fréquent chez le chien, représentant 85% de tous les cancers osseux canins. Ce cancer, très agressif, est à l’origine de fractures pathologiques et de douleur aigüe. La durée de survie moyenne de l’animal sans traitement se situe entre 4 et 5 mois et moins de 10% des chiens atteints d’ostéosarcome survivent 1 an.
L’ostéosarcome est actuellement traité par amputation ou par des chirurgies conservatrices des membres associées à de la chimiothérapie, qui permettent d’augmenter la survie à 1 an jusqu’à 50 %(2). Toutefois, 50% des chiens survivant 1 an et plus grâce à ces traitements sont susceptibles de développer des métastases, avec une espérance de survie médiane ne dépassant pas 9 mois(3).
Dans certain cas, l’amputation n’est pas la meilleure option, en particulier pour les chiens de grande ou très grande race, surtout s’ils souffrent de troubles neurologiques ou orthopédiques concomitants (dysplasie, maladie dégénérative articulaire...).
En outre, les propriétaires de ces animaux recherchent de plus en plus souvent des traitements palliatifs afin d’éviter l’amputation. Enfin, les chirurgies conservatrices ayant recours à des endoprothèses et des allogreffes d’os cortical sont des procédures complexes, non applicables à tous les sites affectés et qui peuvent entrainer des complicatios majeures. Il existe donc un véritable besoin de nouvelles techniques alternatives.
Au cours des dernières années, le Professeur Olivier Gauthier, Professeur de chirurgie des petits animaux et dentisterie vétérinaire, a mis au point une technique de chirurgie conservatrice mini-invasive consistant en l’injection de ciment phosphocalcique au niveau du site tumoral.
Les résultats de ces travaux précurseurs ont ainsi montré qu’une telle technique permet de conserver la fonction du membre et de soulager immédiatement et durablement la douleur, améliorant ainsi considérablement le bien-être de l’animal.
【5†Image: ostéosarcomes appendiculaires chez le chien】
### L'étude clinique menée à Oniris
#### 【6†Découvrir l'étude】
  * La phase de recrutement est actuellement ouverte à Oniris. Elle consiste à inclure des chiens atteints d’ostéosarcome appendiculaire.
  * Une dizaine de chien ont déjà été traités avec succès par cette méthode.
  * L’injection du ciment phosphocalcique à l’intérieur de l’os rongé par la tumeur. se fait par voie percutanée sous anesthésie générale et sous contrôle radioscopique. Elle ne nécessite pas d’intervention massive. Une incision de la peau sur deux centimètres suffit, à introduire la canule dans l’os.
### Qui peut participer à l'étude clinique réalisée à Oniris ?

Le recrutement s’adresse aux propriétaires de chiens de grande race et de race géante atteints d’un ostéosarcome appendiculaire diagnostiqué par imagerie. En cas de doute sur la nature tumorale de la lésion osseuse, une biopsie osseuse pourra être réalisée.

【7†Image: ostéosarcome appendiculaire diagnostiqué par imagerie】
### Quels sont les avantages du traitement innovant proposé à Oniris ?
  * Cette étude offre une solution à des propriétaires qui, confrontés à la grave maladie de leur chien, recherchent des traitements palliatifs, et veulent éviter l’amputation et agir pour le bien-être de leur animal.
  * Cette méthode assure une fin de vie la plus confortable possible et soulage grandement la douleur dans les deniers mois.
  * Ce traitement  peut permettre d’éviter l’euthanasie précoce de l’animal, parfois la seule solution qui s’offre au propriétaire face à la souffrance de son animal.

What is a Clinical Trial?
A clinical trial is a research study in which animals with cancer participate to evaluate aspects of, or novel treatments for, cancer. Well-designed clinical trials can answer questions about preventing, detecting, and treating cancer that help many animals in the future. Trials are designed to minimize risk to the participants, but drug trials often involve new anti-cancer agents that may not have been used in companion animals, and the extent of possible toxicity is not known.
There are four phases of clinical trials to safely and methodically evaluate promising new treatments.
Phase 1 trials are typically conducted in a small group of animals (6-12) with cancer to test a new treatment that has never been tried in a clinical patient. The goals are to evaluate safety and side effects, and to determine the dose and way to use the treatment. It is important to remember that no therapeutic benefit is expected in a phase 1 trial.
Phase 2 trials use information from phase 1 trials to use the new treatment at a given dose and schedule in a larger group of animals with cancer (usually 20-40). The goal of a phase 2 trial is to determine efficacy of the new treatment and further evaluate safety. In cancer clinical trials, a phase 2 trial is intended to determine what types of cancer will respond or how well a given cancer responds to a new therapy.

# Clinical Trials for Dogs with Cancer

Links last verified: August 20, 2026
## Explore Current Research Trials in Canine Oncology

When a beloved dog is diagnosed with cancer, many families ask whether a clinical trial may provide an additional option. Canine oncology studies are conducted throughout the United States and around the world, but identifying an appropriate trial, and participating in one, can sometimes be challenging.

Each clinical trial has specific eligibility requirements.

These may include:
  * A dog’s breed
  * Age
  * Weight
  * Overall health
  * Life expectancy
  * Cancer type
  * Cancer stage
  * Previous care
  * ...and other medical factors

Meeting a study’s general description does not guarantee acceptance. Pet parents should speak directly with the research team and their veterinary care provider to determine whether a trial may be appropriate for their dog.

It is also important to understand that clinical trials are not always free.
Research funding may cover only certain tests, medications, procedures, or appointments. Families may still be responsible for additional veterinary expenses, travel, lodging, and repeated visits over several weeks or months, especially when a study is located far from home.

The following links are intended to help pet parents and veterinary professionals find information about current canine oncology trials being conducted throughout the United States and, in some cases, internationally.
We encourage families to carefully review each study’s eligibility requirements, location, potential costs, time commitment, and possible benefits and risks with their veterinary team.

## Start Here: Nationwide Search Tools

If you are not sure where to begin, start with the AVMA registry. It lets you search by cancer type and by location, which is faster than checking individual centers one at a time.
#### 【64†AVMA Veterinary Clinical Trials Registry†veterinaryclinicaltrials.org】

The AVMA Veterinary Clinical Trials Registry, formerly known as the AVMA Animal Health Studies Database, helps dog parents and veterinary professionals find veterinary clinical studies taking place throughout the United States and Canada. By making this information easier to access, the registry supports continued research and progress in veterinary medicine and canine health care.
If you are interested in a clinical trial for your dog, begin by discussing the study and your dog’s potential eligibility with your veterinary care provider.



【64†AVMA Clinical Trials†veterinaryclinicaltrials.org】
#### 【66†National Cancer Institute, Comparative Oncology Program†ccr.cancer.gov】

The Comparative Oncology Program develops and conducts clinical trials in partnership with veterinary teaching institutions throughout the United States. Dogs enrolled in these studies receive care from board-certified veterinary oncologists committed to improving comfort, quality of life, and cancer care for companion animals.
The knowledge gained through this research may help advance the understanding of cancer and support future progress in both canine and human oncology.

【66†National Cancer Institute†ccr.cancer.gov】
#### 【67†PetCure Oncology†petcureoncology.com】

PetCure Oncology provides stereotactic radiation surgery and stereotactic radiation therapy, commonly known as SRS and SRT. These highly precise forms of radiation therapy have been used in human oncology and are now available for dogs with certain types of cancer.
PetCure Oncology reports using SRS and SRT in thousands of companion animals with a variety of tumor types. Its affiliated veterinary specialists continue to study these approaches to better understand their potential benefits, safety considerations, side effects, and appropriate applications in canine cancer care.

## Keep in Mind

Clinical trials may explore new approaches to diagnosing or supporting dogs with cancer. These may include chemotherapy, radiation therapy, surgical procedures, temperature-based therapies, immunotherapy, photodynamic therapy, and other emerging approaches.
Although many clinical trials take place at veterinary colleges and teaching hospitals, a growing number of specialty and referral practices also participate in canine cancer research. Some studies require every appointment to be completed at the participating institution, while others may allow certain tests, procedures, or follow-up visits to be handled by a dog’s regular veterinary team.
The words “experimental” and “investigational” can understandably feel concerning. Before a new therapy or procedure reaches a veterinary clinical trial, researchers have typically completed earlier stages of evaluation. However, unknowns may remain regarding its safety, effectiveness, or potential side effects. A study is offered because researchers believe the approach may provide meaningful benefits, but participation does not guarantee a positive outcome.
Pet parents should review the study’s purpose, requirements, possible benefits, known and unknown risks, costs, and available alternatives with the clinical trial team and their dog’s veterinary care provider before making a decision.

## 新規の治療・臨床試験のご紹介
### 猫変形性関節症に関するスクリーニング調査について

本院では、研究の一環として、猫変形性関節症に関するスクリーニング調査を実施しており、参加していただける猫を募集しています。

猫では変形性関節症の発症が多く、それらの猫は痛みを感じながら生活していると考えられます。どの程度の猫で変形性関節症がみられ、その症状が獣医学的に検出可能であるかどうか確認すること、また関節に良いとされるサプリメントを使用して症状がどの程度管理されるかを判定することを目的としています。

本調査では当院に来院される猫を含め、同居猫、知人の猫など、全年齢、全ての猫を対象としています。特に高齢の猫では変形性関節症が多くみられるため、積極的な参加をお願いいたします。

今回用いるサプリメントはエランコジャパン（株）製のアンセットとリナイス（株）製のサケ鼻軟骨抽出物です。
当院へ来院された猫に関しては主治医の同意が得られた場合に限りますが、一度ご相談ください。サプリメントは無償で供与され、また検査費用はかかりませんが、サプリメントの使用前および使用後に2度の検査のため本院へ来院が必要であり、サプリメントを1ヶ月毎日服用していただく必要がございます。



詳細は北海道大学動物医療センター整形外科担当　奥村・須永までお問い合わせください。 Tel 011-706-5239 (8:30〜17:00)

→ 【49†ポスター】
### 抗PD-L1抗体による腫瘍免疫療法について（臨床研究）

本院では、北海道大学獣医学研究院にて開発したイヌ用抗体医薬「抗PD-L1抗体」によるイヌの腫瘍疾患の試験的治療（臨床研究）を行っており、研究へ参加していただける患者さんを募集しています。

本治療薬は免疫チェックポイント阻害剤と呼ばれる新しい免疫療法薬であり、ヒト医療における抗PD-1抗体（ニボルマブ、ペンブロリズマブ）や抗PD-L1抗体（アテゾリズマブ、デュルバルマブ）と同様の作用機序を持ちます。

本試験では、肺転移を有する口腔内悪性黒色腫をはじめとしたイヌの悪性腫瘍を対象としています。

動物の状態などについて制限がありますが、まずは一度ご相談ください。本院に定期的に通院していただく必要があること、安全性や有効性評価のための定期検査にご同意いただく必要があることにご留意ください。



詳細は、臨床研究担当者（獣医学研究院　今内 覚）までメールにてお問い合わせください。

→ huvcr■vetmed.hokudai.ac.jp　（■を@に換えて送信してください）

## 北海道大学大学院獣医学研究院 臨床研究推進研究費

獣医学研究院および北海道大学動物医療センターでは獣医学の発展に向けた研究を支援するべく、臨床研究推進研究費による研究支援を行っています。



本研究費は、臨床系教員と臨床系ではない教員が目的に応じて共同研究チームを構築して、動物医療センターを舞台とした臨床研究の活性化を図り、トランスレーショナルリサーチの推進および One Health / Zoobiquity の推進を目指すことを目的としています。

# COOL - Clinical Trials

At the Comparative Oral Oncology Laboratory (COOL), our research bridges discovery and clinical patient care. Through targeted clinical trials, we offer novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for companion animals facing oral cancers.
## Active Trial: Novel Targeted Oral Therapy for Canine Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma (OSCC)

Squamous Cell Carcinoma is the second most common oral malignancy in dogs. Because these tumors are locally invasive, rapidly erode bone, and frequently recur following conventional treatments, surgical options are sometimes limited.
This study evaluates Trametinib, an FDA-approved targeted oral medication used in human oncology. Having established its safety in dogs, our goal in this expanded trial is to identify specific molecular and genetic profiles that predict favorable treatment response, allowing us to deliver precise, effective targeted therapy.

Eligibility: Dogs presented to or evaluated through the Cornell University Hospital for Animals (CUHA) with a biopsy-confirmed or strongly suspected oral squamous cell carcinoma.
Financial Coverage: All diagnostic imaging, physical exams, sedation, follow-up procedures, and trial medications required during the study are provided free of charge. Additionally, dogs that complete the 126-day protocol receive an additional $1,000 credit toward standard-of-care follow-up therapy.

Owner Commitment: Administer oral medication once daily at home (chemotherapy handling and safety guidance provided).
Bring your dog to CUHA for scheduled re-checks on or around Days 14, 42, 70, 108, and 126.

Complete short weekly health status surveys (via phone or in-person during visits).

Final Evaluation (Day 126): Includes a physical exam, full-body CT scan under general anesthesia to document treatment response, tumor biopsy, and fine-needle aspirates of mandibular lymph nodes for genomic analysis.

Study Leadership: Santiago Peralta, DVM, Dipl. AVDC, Founding Fellow AVDC-OMFS
Sponsor: Funded by the Cornell Richard P. Riney Canine Health Center.

How to Enroll or Refer a Patient: If you are a dog owner interested in screening, or a veterinarian seeking to refer a patient for trial evaluation:

Phone: (607) 253-3060 (Request the Dentistry & Oral Surgery or Oncology Service)

Email: vet-research@cornell.edu

Location: Cornell University Hospital for Animals, Ithaca, NY

Mission
## Designer cell therapies for pets first — and their people next.

When a pet gets sick, families face limited options. LEAH Labs is changing that. We combine world-class gene editing with novel protein engineering to revolutionize companion animal oncology — while generating the insights that will power the next generation of human CAR-T therapies.

> Translational medicine is in our DNA.

1st ever
We're the first, and only, in the world to put pets in remissions using CAR-T cell therapy in dogs with cancer.

The only CAR-T cell therapy company for dogs

World leading vets are testing CAR-T cells in pets, but we're the only ones doing this commercially.

Our trials are fully funded

We cover 100% of the costs for pet parents who enroll in our trials

Science
## Purpose built for pets.
Advanced enough for humans.

Four pillars. One platform.

01

### Generative Biology & De Novo Protein Engineering

Leveraging breakthroughs in AI and protein design, LEAH Labs designs, builds, and tests novel therapeutic assets that didn't evolve in nature. We're not iterating on legacy biology — we're inventing new biology from first principles.

02
### Precision Gene Editing — GeneWeld

Our founder invented our gene editing platform during their PhD. This platform is a critical enabling technology that allows us to build CAR-T cell therapies at costs affordable to pet parents.

03
### Harnessing Immune Cells to Fight Cancer

The immune system can detect and destroy cancer — but cancer evades it. Gene editing lets us reprogram T cells to become professional cancer-fighting assassins. CAR-T cell therapy is already curative in human blood cancers. We're bringing it their furry family members.

04
### Canine Translational Oncology

Dogs develop the same spontaneous cancers as humans, in a shared environment, with a fully intact immune system. Disease in dogs mirrors disease in people. Every remission in a dog is a data point that accelerates human medicine — compressing timelines that would otherwise take a decade.

# OCTOBER 2025

Retrospective evaluation of impact of lymphadenectomy on survival of dogs with cutaneous mast cell tumors.

Lead investigator: Dr. Mirja Nolff (Clinic of Small Animal Surgery, Vetsuisse Zürich, University of Zürich, Switzerland).

Aim and objectives:
The aim of this study is, to assess the impact of nodal management on outcome in dogs with grade 2/low grade mast cell tumors that are solely treated by surgical intervention. Furthermore, we want to assess if SLN based resection results in a superior outcome compared to regional lymphadenectomy. Our hypothesis is, that lymphadenectomy will result in improved survival time compared to cases were lymph-nodes were not treated in both species.
Furthermore, we propose that this effect will be more pronounced in dogs when SLN mapping was used to determine the nodes to be resected.
Please contact Dr. Nolff (mnolff@vetclinics.uzh.ch) for more details.

# Trials clinici in Oncologia Veterinaria

Al fine di far progredire la conoscenza sulle malattie oncologiche che colpiscono i nostri animali da compagnia, i medici veterinari che operano presso l’Ospedale Veterinario dell’Università di Bologna conducono studi clinici volti a valutare l’efficacia di nuove indagini diagnostiche e strategie terapeutiche. Queste scoperte possono spesso essere applicate alla medicina in tutte le specie.
La maggior parte delle ricerche condotte presso il nostro Ospedale si basa sull’applicazione clinica di protocolli innovativi e promettenti sulla base di dati preliminari ottenuti in laboratorio. L’inclusione nello studio consente al paziente di ricevere, a basso costo, un trattamento potenzialmente vantaggioso e superiore rispetto alla terapia attualmente disponibile, con risvolti positivi anche per i futuri malati.
Tutti gli studi clinici sono avviati solo dopo il ricevimento di un parere favorevole da parte del Comitato Etico-Scientifico dell’Università.
Il personale medico discute con il proprietario dell’animale i requisiti necessari all’arruolamento in uno specifico protocollo di ricerca, elencandone i vantaggi, i rischi e le opportunità per quel paziente specifico. In caso di inclusione nello studio, il proprietario provvede alla firma di un consenso informato alle indagini e ai trattamenti sul proprio animale.

Clinical research is an important component of increasing medical knowledge, advancing veterinary practice, and improving animal health. The College of Veterinary Medicine routinely conducts clinical trials as a component of that research. Our studies are open to patients of the Veterinary Hospital and beyond. If you are a veterinarian or owner with an animal diagnosed with a condition being researched and are interested in enrolling them in the trial, contact the department or lab associated with the research to see if your animal qualifies.

## What You Need to Know About Clinical Trials

【189†What is a clinical trial?】
Clinical studies are biomedical or health-related investigations in animals or human beings that attempt to answer a question in a systematic way. As such, they often are used to evaluate risk factors for disease, as well as methods to prevent, treat or cure disease.
A clinical trial is one type of clinical study that involves testing the effects of a new or existing treatment (drug, medical device, behavioral change etc) on an illness or disorder or a new diagnostic test to help develop early diagnostics or prognostic information.
【190†Why are clinical trials important?】
Extensive laboratory research precedes the initiation of a clinical trial. The treatment or diagnostic test in question will have been evaluated in a laboratory setting and promising results obtained that support its further evaluation in a clinical trial. As laboratory investigations cannot accurately predict how an individual with naturally occurring disease will respond to the treatment, a clinical trial must be performed to identify how safe and effective a treatment is for its intended use.
Many clinical trials in the veterinary field involve treatments that have already been proven safe and effective in humans with similar disease. However, since animals differ from humans in many ways – including how they may respond to specific treatment – veterinary based clinical trials are needed to determine the most appropriate treatment for our pets.
【191†What are the benefits of participating in a clinical trial?】

Participation in a clinical trial allows the patient to gain access to new research before it is widely available as well as obtain expert veterinary medical care during the trial. In addition, there may be financial incentives for enrolling in a clinical trial, including free veterinary care, testing and treatment. Participants in clinical trials are also helping others by contributing to the advancement of medical research.
【192†Are there risks involved in participating in a clinical trial?】
The experimental treatment may not be effective for the participant, and may be associated with side effects. In addition, participation in a clinical trial may involve multiple visits to the study site for treatment and follow-up; more so than if the patient were not involved in a clinical trial. The specific requirements of each study as well as potential study associated risks are detailed in the Informed Consent document. This document must be signed prior to participation in a clinical trial.
However, informed consent is not a contract, and the participant may withdraw from the trial at any time. To help ensure the safety of study participants, all clinical trials performed at the Veterinary Teaching Hospital must be approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) at North Carolina State University.
【193†Am I compensated for participating in a trail?】

Information here about financial, and other, incentives for participating in a trial.

【194†Where does financial support come from?】
The College’s research activities are supported by a variety of means. The state of North Carolina provides base support for the research programs, but most research activity is funded through competitive grants from national agencies such as the Morris Animal Foundation, Winn Feline Foundation, Grayson Jockey Fund and the National Institutes of Health as well as through grants, contracts or memoranda of agreement with private companies, foundations and other agencies.

# Oncology Clinical Trials
## What are clinical trials?

Clinical trials are a type of research.  They are an important component of all specialties of medicine and help us as researchers and veterinarians to evaluate new types of diagnostics and treatments.  Clinical trials are variable and may be designed to answer different questions including is a new treatment more effective, is a new diagnostic more specific, or does a new therapy combination have less side effects.
## Who can join clinical trials?
The Lois Bates Acheson Veterinary Teaching Hospital has many clinical trials underway at any one time.  It is possible that a pet may be eligible for more than one ongoing clinical trial.  There are often initial tests such as a physical exam, blood work and/or imaging that are needed to ensure a patient is approved for enrollment in a trial.  All clinical trials have a unique set of inclusion and exclusion criteria that help the research team enroll the correct patient population.  Your pet’s oncology clinicians will discuss standard treatment and clinical trial treatment options with you.  It is your decision as to whether or not you would like your pet to participate in a clinical trial.
## What are the benefits of participating in a clinical trial?

There are several important benefits to participating in clinical trials.  You and your pet will be personally involved in expanding the scientific knowledge of oncology in veterinary patients.  Your pet may also receive novel diagnostics and/or treatments, and may receive these services at reduced or no cost.  The potential benefits of a clinical trial are varied and would be discussed thoroughly prior to your pet’s enrollment.
## Contact information:

Please do not hesitate to contact the teaching hospital and the oncology service for more information on clinical trials.  If your pet has been diagnosed with cancer, we are available to discuss clinical trial options with your referring veterinarian in more detail.

## Current Trials

### Pilot Study Evaluating the Microbiota in Dogs with Lymphoma
#### Study Purpose:
  * The gut microbiome is essential in maintaining the health and immunity of the host.  Alterations in this population of microorganisms and in mucosal tolerance have been shown to be a potential driver in the pathogenesis of many infectious and inflammatory diseases as well as certain types of cancer.
Specifically related to cancer, the human and canine gut microbiota has an active role in drug pharmacokinetics, cancer therapies, and related toxicities.  Limited data exists in the veterinary literature related to the microbiome in dogs diagnosed with lymphoma.
  * The goal of this study is to evaluate differences in the microbiota between healthy dogs, dogs with lymphoma, and dogs with lymphoma treated with chemotherapy. Additionally, the impact of chemotherapy on the microbiota and eventual relapse will be examined. Evaluation of this information will determine whether changes in the microbiota after treatment is a significant prognostic factor for adverse effects from chemotherapy, response to therapy and response duration.
#### Inclusion Criteria:

  * Dogs diagnosed with naïve multicentric lymphoma
  * Dogs at least 1 year of age and minimum weight of 15 kilograms
  * Dogs must be otherwise healthy, and have adequate bone marrow and organ function
  * Owners must sign consent form

#### Exclusion Criteria:

  * Dogs that previously received chemotherapy and/or radiation therapy for lymphoma treatment
  * Concurrent malignancy or other serious systemic disorder incompatible with this study
#### Study Protocol:
  * Dogs will need a physical exam, complete blood count, serum biochemistry, and confirmation of lymphoma and immunophenotype to ensure eligibility for enrollment.
  * Dogs must be treated with either the 19- week CHOP or single agent doxorubicin chemotherapy protocol

## About BluePearl Science.

Founded by our dedicated clinicians, BluePearl Science coordinates clinical studies to increase medical knowledge, advance veterinary practice and develop new diagnostic and treatment approaches that offer novel and potentially lifesaving options for pets.

【1†Image: Pictured Jaime Rechy Jr, DVM, DACVR】

【2†Watch on YouTube†www.youtube.com】

## Our goals.
### Creating a better future for pets.

Innovative diagnostic and treatment solutions and pharmaceuticals can save pets' lives.

Assessing the effectiveness of drugs, diagnostics and procedures through clinical studies can help protect and promote the lives of pets today and tomorrow.

【3†Image: ...】
### Sharing knowledge and expertise with the community.

We believe veterinarians can make the greatest impact when we work together.

Performing clinical studies to gain knowledge about new medical treatment options is part of our service to the national veterinary community. Data from these studies are published in peer-reviewed literature, allowing everyone to benefit from the findings.

【4†Image: Veterinary Ophthalmologist Surgery】
### Coordinating with primary care veterinarians.

Our emergency and specialty clinicians share a common goal with primary care veterinarians: To provide exceptional care for your pet.

When your pet is involved in a clinical study at BluePearl, we will always keep your family veterinarian informed when it comes to diagnostic and treatment plans.

【5†Image: Maia Derm Reiter】
### Collaborating with pet families.

Pets benefit from novel diagnostic or therapeutic options as part of BluePearl's clinical studies program and pet families are involved in every care decision along the way.

In all cases, both traditional and investigational treatments will be discussed so pet families can make informed care decisions for their specific circumstances.
【6†Image: Tina Fargo, an ophthalmology tech in the Tampa hospital, receives a kiss from patient Louie. Louie is an English Bulldog who had entropion eye surgery.】

【7†Image: 】
## Frequently asked questions.

What is a clinical study?

Clinical studies are an important way of increasing medical knowledge, advancing veterinary practice and improving animal health.

Clinical studies at our hospitals can be sponsored by veterinarians or granting agencies seeking new ways to diagnose and treat disease in veterinary patients, by other groups within the Mars Petcare Ecosystem, and by pharmaceutical and technology companies developing new approaches to improve pet care.
What benefits do clinical studies offer me and my pet?

By voluntarily participating in a clinical study, your pet may get access to new approaches to diagnosis and treatment of their condition not available outside the clinical studies setting. Participating in clinical studies also helps provide information that can benefit future pets with similar conditions.
The best interests of the pet, the desires of the pet’s owner, and the mutually agreed upon course of treatment between the owner and veterinarian set the standard of care for both routine veterinary treatment and clinical studies at BluePearl Hospitals.

No pet is ever enrolled in a clinical study at BluePearl without the owner’s fully informed and written consent.

Can healthy pets participate in clinical studies?
For some clinical studies, healthy animals might be able to participate, particularly when there is a need to compare information about healthy pets to pets with a particular disease.

When healthy pets are involved, study activities are non-invasive and might include things like bloodwork or observational assessments (those that just involve looking at the pet).

The Mars Petcare Biobank is an important example of how healthy pets can make a substantial difference in veterinary healthcare studies.
How can my pet become involved?

If you believe that your pet may benefit from enrollment in a clinical study, please contact your family veterinarian.

Below is a complete list of studies currently happening at BluePearl hospitals. There, you'll find more information about qualifications.

For questions about specific studies, you can also reach out to the study contact listed to discuss your pet’s eligibility.

How does BluePearl ensure studies are conducted safely and ethically?
Enrollment in a clinical study is always up to the pet owner and our informed consent process for clinical studies ensures that owners are fully aware of the study's objectives, any potential risks and study requirements before they agree to allow their pets to participate. Owners always sign a written consent form before their pet is enrolled in a study.
As part of the Mars Veterinary Health family of brands, BluePearl Science strictly adheres to the Mars Policy on Clinical Studies. Clinical studies at BluePearl undergo a rigorous review process to ensure the highest medical and ethical care standards for all pets and their owners.
This process is conducted by our Veterinary Clinical Studies Committee (VCSC), comprised of individuals with specific expertise in clinical medicine and surgery, clinical and basic research, animal welfare and regulatory issues, the human-animal bond and social work, and members of the community not affiliated with BluePearl or Mars.
I’m interested in sponsoring or collaborating on a clinical study. How can I work with BluePearl hospitals?
BluePearl Science leverages one of the world’s largest private providers of specialty and emergency veterinary care to advance new and exciting diagnostics and treatments for our veterinary patients. We coordinate clinical studies across a national network of 100+ hospitals. BluePearl Science carries out collaborative research only with institutions that comply with our animal welfare and ethical standards, and we welcome the opportunity to discuss your upcoming project.
Contact us at 【8†[email protected]】.

# Veterinary Clinical Trials

Clinical trials at VROC help evaluate new cancer treatments for pets by assessing their safety, effectiveness, and potential side effects. Participation is entirely voluntary, and the decision to enroll your pet is yours. However, enrollment in a clinical trial is required for a patient to be seen in our clinic.
Our studies build upon the current standard of care using the same advanced technologies available in leading specialty pet cancer hospitals. While specific outcomes cannot be guaranteed, our team is committed to providing the highest standard of veterinary oncology care throughout each trial.

For questions or to learn more about available studies, please contact Paige Neumann, Research Study Coordinator, at 214-645-6221 or by VROC@UTSouthwestern.edu (no-reply@utsouthwestern.edu).
## Current Trials
### Brain cancer clinical trials for dogs and cats

Safety and Therapeutic Efficacy of CAR-Neutrophils Combined with Radiation in Dogs with Glioma: This trial will evaluate the combination of CAR-neutrophils with radiation in dogs with glioma to induce tumor shrinkage and improve overall survival. 【32†View trial】
Safety and Efficacy of Ferumoxytol in Combination with Radiation Therapy in Dogs with Glioma: This trial will evaluate the combination of ferumoxytol with radiation in glioma-bearing canines for reprogramming the tumor microenvironment, inducing tumor cell destruction, and improving radiation therapy. 【33†View trial】
### Other cancer clinical trials for dogs and cats

Veterinary Clinical Trials in Canine Patients Using Combination Novel Therapeutics, Devices, and Data Collection Techniques: This trial will utilize focused ultrasound (FUS), radiotherapy, novel drug combinations, immunotherapy and other therapeutic techniques to treat canines and felines with spontaneous tumors. 【34†View trial】
Evaluation of Weekly Intratumoral Cow Pea Mosaic Virus (CPMV) in Dogs with Solid Tumors: This trial will assess the safety, feasibility, and immunotherapeutic effects of intratumoral administration of CPMV in dogs with naturally occurring solid tumors. 【35†View trial】
Radiation and Histotripsy in Dogs and Cats with Solid Tumors: This trial will assess the safety and tumor response of combined radiation therapy (RT) and high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) histotripsy in dogs with naturally occurring soft tissue sarcoma. 【36†View trial】
Evaluation of Calreticulin-Nanoparticles (CRT-NP) and HIFU Immunotherapy with or without Anti-PD-L1 in Canine Melanoma: This trial will evaluate the anti-tumor immunity of CRT-NP-based immunotherapy combined with HIFU, with or without anti-PD-L1 therapy, in dogs with advanced, naturally occurring melanoma. 【37†View trial】
Intratumoral vs. Intravenous Carboplatin +/- HIFU in Canine Melanoma: This trial will assess the safety, tumor response, and delivery of carboplatin administered intratumorally (nanoparticle/microparticle formulation) vs. intravenously with or without HIFU enhancement.
【38†View trial】
Prospective Non-Randomized Single-Arm Compassionate-Use Protocol for Advanced Non-Resectable Tumors in Dogs and Cats: This trial will evaluate tolerability, quality of life, and tumor immunomodulation in dogs and cats treated with investigational therapy, chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and combination approaches. 【39†View trial】

# Clinical Studies

A clinical study is a carefully designed investigation used to evaluate certain aspects of the diagnosis or treatment of a specific medical condition. The goal is to find new and better ways to prevent, diagnose or treat diseases of dogs and cats. MedVet’s Clinical Studies Center facilitates high-quality clinical studies to advance the veterinary profession in caring for our beloved pets.
## Current Clinical Studies

We have successfully completed single center and multi-center clinical studies evaluating diagnostic tests, pharmaceuticals, biologics, surgical procedures, and medical devices for acute and chronic pain, congestive heart failure and other cardiac diseases, osteoarthritis and other orthopedic diseases, cancer, seizure disorders, endocrine diseases, ophthalmologic conditions, and chronic skin diseases. You can explore our current clinical studies below.
### Experimental EGFR/HER2 Tumor Vaccine

This is a USDA regulated scientific study. Enrollment is limited to dogs with osteosarcoma, hemangiosarcoma and transitional cell carcinoma. The
vaccine is currently provided at no charge to the pet owners. As this is not a fully funded study, all costs associated with hospital visits, diagnostics and vaccine administration are the responsibility of the pet owner. If the vaccine receives approval, it will no longer be provided at no cost.
To ensure all patients meet the enrollment criteria of having an expected prognosis that is greater than three months, MedVet hospitals are currently limiting enrollment to patients who are receiving appropriate standard of care therapies which may include surgery, chemotherapy, and/or radiation therapy depending on the tumor type. Patients being screened for enrollment with the intent to use the vaccine as a single agent treatment will not be considered.
#### Study Locations

  * MedVet Salt Lake City is currently enrolling patients.
  * MedVet Cincinnati and MedVet Cleveland enrollment is limited to established patients with all treatment and follow-up visits being held at the same hospital.
  * MedVet Pittsburgh enrollment is limited to dogs that live in Pennsylvania with all follow up visits being held at MedVet Pittsburgh.
  * MedVet Chicago is currently pausing enrollment until further notice.
#### Study Enrollment Criteria
  * Histologically (biopsy) confirmed diagnosis of osteosarcoma, hemangiosarcoma, or transitional cell carcinoma. An exception may be made if the dog has a long bone (limb) lesion consistent with osteosarcoma and the owner has elected not to pursue amputation. If amputation is planned, the first dose of vaccine can be administered following the amputation.
  * Anticipated survival of greater than 3 months as determined by the evaluating oncologist. While dogs with metastases may be enrolled in the study, this will be based on the extent/volume of disease and prognosis.
  * Dogs cannot be enrolled if they are receiving other immunotherapies or alternative therapies or are enrolled in another clinical study. Traditional chemotherapy and radiation therapy are allowed.
#### Required Testing
  * All costs associated with evaluation and testing are the responsibility of the pet owner and are not covered by the study. You will be provided with a cost estimate for all required and any additional recommended testing.
  * Chest X-rays, CBC, biochemical profile, and urinalysis at baseline prior to vaccine administration. Testing completed within seven days will likely be acceptable.
  * Chest X-rays must be repeated at three, six, and nine months.
  * A blood sample will be collected at each visit (baseline, day 21, day 40-50, three months, six months, nine months) for research purposes.
  * Strict adherence to the vaccine administration guidelines is required. A booster vaccine must be given 21 days following the initial dose. It is allowable to administer the booster one day early or up to seven days late if necessary due to appointment availability or if the administration day falls on a weekend or holiday.
#### Contacts

For questions, e-mail clinicalstudies@medvet.com.

### Immune-mediated Keratoconjunctivitis Sicca ("Dry Eye")

【71†MedVet Columbus】 is currently enrolling dogs diagnosed with immune-mediated Keratoconjunctivitis sicca (“dry eye”) in a clinical study evaluating the use of an investigational new drug in the treatment of KCS in dogs.
#### Study Eligibility
  * Dogs must be ≥ 6 months old
  * Diagnosis of KCS based on history and/or ophthalmic examination
  * Schirmer Tear Test (STT) of ≥ 2 mm/minute and ≤ 10 mm/minute in one or both eyes
  * Dogs must have a score of 2 or above on at least 2 of the 3 conjunctival signs associated with KCS
  * Pet owner must be willing to comply with the protocol restrictions and the visit schedule
  * Dogs with chronic medical conditions (for example, endocrinopathies, cardiovascular conditions, atopy, etc.) are permitted, but such conditions must be stabilized prior to enrolling the dog in the study and these animals must not be receiving prohibited concomitant medications
#### Exclusion Criteria
  * Dogs with non-KCS ophthalmic conditions that require one or more ophthalmic medications (e.g., glaucoma)
  * Dog diagnosed with KCS at < 6 months of age in order to exclude dogs that may have congenital alacrima
  * Suspected neurogenic KCS
  * History of removal of the third eyelid gland in the affected eye(s)
  * KCS associated with a diagnosis of canine distemper
  * History of parotid duct transposition in the affected eye(s)
  * Punctal plugs in the affected eye(s)
  * Non-healed corneal ulcers
  * History of local radiation therapy in the ocular region
  * Other exclusion criteria not listed above will be discussed with you, include certain prohibited concomitant medication
#### Study Information
Your dog will be screened to confirm that it fulfills the inclusion/exclusion criteria for this study. During screening, procedures include obtaining medical history, physical examination, blood and urine collection, obtaining a body weight, and an eye examination will be performed. This is a randomized, masked, negatively-controlled trial. Your dog will be randomly assigned to receive the investigational drug or a negative control product (sterile buffered saline).
Neither you nor your veterinarian will be aware of whether your pet is assigned to receive the investigational drug or negative control product. Patients will be randomly assigned based on order of eligibility for enrollment to one of the two treatment groups in a 2:1 ratio of investigational drug to negative control product.
If your dog is enrolled in the study, you, the owner/undersigned, will be asked to administer treatments to your dog pursuant to Sponsor’s instructions, which will be provided by your veterinarian.
#### Pet Owner Savings
Your dog will receive treatment under this study, including all tests, procedures, and medications, at no cost to you. If your dog has an allergic reaction or is injured as a result of participating in the study, the Sponsor will work with your veterinarian to cover reasonable expenses related to treatment of such reaction or injury. There are no additional expenses for participating in this study.
If your pet is excluded or removed from the study, but requires continued care for eye disease, future examinations and procedures will NOT be covered by the research study. An estimate of costs for which you will be responsible will be prepared for you at the time of admission.
#### Contact

If you are interested in the study and would like to learn more, please reach out to Dr. Terah Webb.­

### Chronic Inflammatory Enteropathy

【72†MedVet Dayton】, 【73†MedVet Mandeville】, and 【74†WestVet Boise】 are currently enrolling dogs with chronic inflammatory enteropathy (CIE) in a clinical study evaluating the effectiveness of an investigational monoclonal antibody.
#### Study Information
Dogs will be screened to confirm that they meet the inclusion/exclusion criteria. Screening diagnostics include upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy with biopsies, blood and fecal testing, and imaging. Patients that qualify will be randomly assigned to receive either the investigational product or a control product (placebo). Pet owners must be willing to commit to the study visit schedule over a 130-day period.
Pet families will be required to assess and record clinical signs of CIE during the study.
#### Study Eligibility
  * Eligible dogs will have a history of chronic, intermittent vomiting, diarrhea, inappetence/anorexia, and/or weight loss for a minimum of three weeks prior to screening.
  * Must not have any other serious concurrent illnesses such as hepatic or renal disease, cancer, diabetes, Addison’s disease, Cushing’s disease, or any other disease that could interfere with the study results.
  * Must not be positive for gastrointestinal (GI) parasites, histoplasmosis, or schistosomiasis at the screening visit.
  * May not have significant panhypoproteinemia and/or marked ascites at the screening visit.
  * May not have evidence of GI obstruction or mass at the time of screening.
  * May not have or suspected of having exocrine pancreatic insufficiency.
  * May not have a history of any surgical procedure in the past 30 days or any GI surgery within the past six months prior to screening.May not be on any prohibited medications within the following time frame prior to screening.
    * One week: Dewormers, anti-diarrheal
    * Two weeks: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS)
    * Four weeks: Short acting steroids, pancreatic enzyme supplements, vaccines, Apoquel
    * 12 weeks: Long-acting steroids, immunosuppressive agents, alkylating agents, Cytopoint
    * Not allowed: Mitotane, Trilostane
#### Pet Owner Savings

This is a funded study that includes testing, procedures, medication, and food (all directly related to this study and its requirements) at no cost to pet owners. In the event of an adverse event, the study sponsor may cover reasonable expenses related to participation.

#### Referral Incentive

Referral partners are eligible for a $200 gift card from the study sponsor for each patient that is screened and enrolled in the study.
